saml.description: Dex ignores the offline_access scope for SAML connector logins and does not issue refresh tokens for SAML-backed sessions.
saml.note: Absence of refresh_token in SAML flows is by design and must not be flagged as a replay or freshness bug.

saml.description: A valid bearer token may be reused across multiple API calls until expiry.
saml.source: RFC 6750 / Dex OAuth2 token usage model
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer token reuse as replay unless the artifact is documented as one-time.

saml.description: Dex access tokens are bearer tokens and may be reused until expiry unless a one-time artifact is explicitly documented.
saml.note: Do not flag ordinary bearer-token reuse as replay for Dex-issued OAuth/OIDC tokens.

saml.description: Acceptance of JWTs without nbf or with future nbf is spec-compliant because nbf is optional.
saml.note: Do not report lack of nbf enforcement alone as a vulnerability.

saml.description: Dex requires sending the initial AuthnRequest and validates InResponseTo; it does not process unprompted SAML AuthnResponses.
saml.note: A forged unsolicited SAMLResponse being rejected is expected behavior, not a flow bug.

saml.description: Admin changes to connector configuration such as SAML trust anchors, issuer expectations, or audience settings are expected to take effect as authorized configuration changes.
saml.note: Do not flag successful logins under newly authorized connector settings as trust-anchor substitution; only stale acceptance under old settings is relevant.

saml.description: Dex uses SAML NameID as the user's unique identifier; username/email/group attributes are mapped as claims but do not replace the principal key.
saml.note: Email or username collisions without NameID collision may be by-design claim overlap rather than identity merge.

saml.description: Admin-created or updated OAuth2 clients via Dex configuration or gRPC are authoritative; subsequent logins using the new client settings are expected.
saml.note: Do not flag behavior changes caused by explicit admin client reconfiguration as coherence bugs.

saml.constraint: Dex's documented dynamic management API is gRPC, not REST. The fuzzer MUST use gRPC methods for create_provider and create_application; do NOT invent HTTP admin endpoints for connector or client creation.

SAML login in Dex is SP-initiated only. Dex must send the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value. The fuzzer MUST initiate the OIDC auth flow first and only then POST the forged SAMLResponse to /callback/{connector_id}; unsolicited SAML responses will be rejected.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens. If offline_access is requested in a SAML-backed login, Dex ignores it. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a failure or freshness bug for SAML flows.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex provides an explicit insecure bypass: insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true skips signature validation. A valid security test MUST leave this option unset/false when testing secure behavior. If login succeeds only with insecureSkipSignatureValidation enabled, that is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure the SAML connector with ssoIssuer. If ssoIssuer is omitted, the docs describe it as optional, so issuer comparison may not be enforced. The fuzzer MUST set ssoIssuer when testing saml_issuer_mismatch; otherwise acceptance may reflect missing configuration rather than a validation flaw.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected SAML audience unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST know which value is authoritative for the configured connector before testing saml_wrong_audience or saml_no_audience_restriction.

For I1 destination-binding tests, if the SAML assertion status contains a Destination element, it must match redirectURI exactly. The fuzzer MUST preserve exact redirectURI matching when crafting SAML responses or failures will be due to destination mismatch rather than the intended invariant.

Dex binds the downstream user identity to the SAML NameID value. The docs state NameID is treated as the user's unique identifier and is assumed unique and immutable. For I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST vary NameID to test principal binding; changing only email or username attributes will not change the core identity binding.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios, nameIDPolicyFormat is a format selector, not a wildcard-capable matcher. It does not support glob or regex semantics. Do NOT attempt to use it as a permissive pattern; choose a stable NameID format and vary actual NameID values across test identities.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is list-membership against asserted group values, not wildcard or regex matching. filterGroups only controls whether non-allowed groups are excluded from claims; it does not change matching semantics. For multi-identity tests requiring different groups to pass the same connector, the fuzzer MUST omit allowedGroups rather than set wildcard-like values.

For I5 group parsing tests, groupsAttr normally expects repeated attributes of the same name. If groupsDelim is configured, Dex instead splits a single string attribute on that delimiter. The fuzzer MUST align the SAML assertion's group encoding with the connector configuration or group-based results will be misinterpreted.

For I2 SAML expiry tests such as saml_expired_assertion, the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid assertion first. Without a control, a failed expired-assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated flow setup, bad connector config, or callback mismatch.

Dex's token exchange flow is documented to work only with OIDC connectors, not SAML connectors. Do NOT attempt to use token_exchange as a SAML upstream test path; SAML protocol tests must use the browser/OIDC front-channel flow ending in the SAML callback.

Dex's /token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies for authorization_code, password, and token-exchange grants, and client credentials are supplied via HTTP Basic authentication in the documented examples. The fuzzer MUST send form-encoded requests and include client credentials as Basic auth where required.

Dex's documented dynamic management API is gRPC, not REST. Application/client creation is available via the gRPC CreateClient method; the docs do not provide REST admin endpoints for creating SAML connectors or users. The fuzzer MUST NOT invent REST setup endpoints for SAML connector provisioning.

Dex SAML connector uses HTTP POST binding. The saml_login operation MUST POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields SAMLResponse and RelayState to /callback/{connector_id}; GET-based callback testing is invalid for this connector.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution, Dex documentation explicitly exposes insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true to skip signature validation. A valid insecure-default test MUST leave insecureSkipSignatureValidation unset/false and then attempt attacker-signed SAMLResponse. If the connector is configured with insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true, acceptance is by configuration and MUST NOT be reported as a vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, Dex only checks the SAML Issuer against configured ssoIssuer when ssoIssuer is set. If ssoIssuer is omitted, issuer comparison may be skipped. The fuzzer MUST run two cases: default-config hardening check with ssoIssuer unset, and enforcement test with ssoIssuer explicitly configured. Do NOT interpret acceptance under unset ssoIssuer as bypass of an enabled check.

For I5 audience-binding tests, Dex uses redirectURI as the expected SAML AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST compute the expected audience from entityIssuer when present, otherwise from redirectURI; using the wrong expected audience will misclassify results.

For I1/I5 destination and audience tests, if the SAML assertion/response contains a Destination element, Dex requires it to match redirectURI exactly. The fuzzer MUST preserve exact callback URL matching when constructing control assertions; otherwise failures may be due to Destination mismatch rather than the intended invariant.

For I4 principal-binding tests, Dex uses the SAML NameID value as the user's unique identifier and assumes it is unique and never changes. The fuzzer MUST treat NameID as the primary upstream identity key for collision tests; usernameAttr/emailAttr mappings affect claims, not the unique principal binding.

For I4 multi-identity scenarios, nameIDPolicyFormat is not a wildcard or pattern-matching field; it selects a concrete SAML NameID format and defaults to persistent. The fuzzer MUST vary actual NameID values, not attempt wildcard matching through nameIDPolicyFormat.

For I5 group-based authorization tests, allowedGroups is list-membership filtering against asserted groups, not wildcard/regex matching. If the fuzzer needs multiple different group values to pass the same connector, it MUST omit allowedGroups or enumerate exact allowed values; setting '*' would be treated as a literal group name, not a wildcard.

For I5 group filtering tests, when filterGroups=true Dex excludes groups not present in allowedGroups from the resulting claims. This can remove groups from downstream tokens without denying login. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'authentication denied because user not in any allowedGroups' from 'login succeeds but extra groups are filtered out' to avoid false escalation findings.

For I2 freshness tests on SAML assertions, Dex docs state it validates InResponseTo and supports no refresh tokens for SAML. The fuzzer MUST include a control SAML login in the same configuration before expired_assertion or replay attempts; otherwise a failed attack login may reflect broken SP-initiated flow setup rather than assertion freshness enforcement.

Dex SAML connector ignores offline_access because SAML does not support non-interactive requery. The fuzzer MUST NOT expect refresh_token issuance after SAML login, and absence of refresh_token is by design rather than an I2 failure.

Dex does not support signed AuthnRequests or encrypted attributes in the SAML connector. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat lack of signed AuthnRequest support or inability to process encrypted attributes as proof-integrity failures in Dex's SAML response validation path.

OAuth2 password grant works only when oauth2.passwordConnector is configured and the password grant is enabled. The fuzzer MUST use login_with_password only for admin/bootstrap scenarios where the local connector is explicitly enabled; otherwise token endpoint failures are expected setup errors.

Dex's documented dynamic management surface is gRPC, not REST. Setup operations such as creating SAML connectors and OAuth clients MUST use the gRPC API when testing dynamic configuration; do not invent REST admin endpoints.

For SAML login tests, the flow MUST be SP-initiated first. Dex sends the initial AuthnRequest and validates the SAML Response InResponseTo value; unsolicited/unprompted AuthnResponses are not accepted.
The SAML connector uses HTTP POST binding. saml_login MUST POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded fields SAMLResponse and RelayState to /callback/{connector_id}; do not use GET.

To test I1 signature-validation defaults, create the SAML connector without insecureSkipSignatureValidation. If insecureSkipSignatureValidation=true is set, signature verification is explicitly disabled for testing and any successful forged assertion is by configuration, not a vulnerability.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure ssoIssuer on the SAML connector. If ssoIssuer is omitted, Dex has no documented expected Issuer value to compare against, so issuer-mismatch tests may pass trivially because issuer binding was never configured.

For I5 audience-binding tests, configure either entityIssuer or redirectURI carefully. Dex uses redirectURI as the expected AudienceRestriction unless entityIssuer is specified, in which case entityIssuer overrides redirectURI as the required audience. The fuzzer MUST target the actual configured audience source when crafting wrong-audience assertions.

For I1 destination-binding tests, if the SAML response contains a Destination element, it must match redirectURI exactly. A mismatch causes rejection for destination reasons, which can mask other invariants under test.

Dex binds the downstream user identity to the SAML NameID value. For I4 multi-identity and collision tests, vary NameID directly; usernameAttr and emailAttr only map auxiliary claims and do not replace NameID as the unique identifier.

nameIDPolicyFormat defaults to persistent if unset. For I4 tests that rely on email-like or transient NameID semantics, the connector configuration MUST explicitly set nameIDPolicyFormat to the intended format; otherwise Dex assumes a persistent identifier.

allowedGroups is list-membership filtering, not wildcard or regex matching. For I4 multi-identity scenarios that need multiple distinct users to pass, do NOT set allowedGroups to '*' or pattern-like values; omit allowedGroups entirely or provide concrete group names that all test identities actually possess.

filterGroups only removes non-allowed groups from the returned claim set; allowedGroups controls admission. For I5 authorization tests, do not confuse claim filtering with authentication gating: a user not in any allowedGroups should be rejected, while filterGroups=true merely trims extra groups.

groupsAttr matching is exact attribute-name lookup only. There is no companion type parameter for glob or regex. For I4/I5 tests, wildcards in groupsAttr would be treated literally; use the exact SAML attribute name or omit group-based tests.

usernameAttr and emailAttr are exact attribute-name mappings only. There is no companion type parameter for pattern matching. For multi-identity tests, do not attempt wildcard attribute names; use exact SAML attribute names.

If groupsDelim is unset, Dex expects multiple groups as repeated attributes with the same name. If groupsDelim is set, Dex expects a single string attribute split by that delimiter. The fuzzer MUST match the configured representation or group-based I4/I5 tests will fail due to parsing differences rather than security behavior.

The SAML connector does not support refresh tokens and ignores offline_access. Tests must not expect a refresh_token from SAML-backed logins, and absence of refresh_token is by design rather than an I2 failure.

For I2 expired-assertion tests, include a control login with a valid assertion before the expired assertion attempt. Otherwise a failed expired assertion login cannot be distinguished from broken SAML connector setup.

Dex's OAuth2 password grant only works when oauth2.passwordConnector is configured and the password grant is enabled. For SAML profiles, login_with_password may be available only for admin/setup access via the local connector; do not assume it authenticates through SAML.
Dex's /token endpoint requires application/x-www-form-urlencoded requests for authorization_code, password, and token-exchange grants. Sending JSON will not exercise the documented flow.

Token exchange at /token is documented only for OIDC upstream connectors, not SAML connectors. Do not run SAML-specific attack oracles through token_exchange and interpret failures or successes as SAML connector behavior.

Dex-issued tokens are client-bound. For I5 audience and cross-client tests, create distinct clients and verify aud/azp behavior using trustedPeers and audience:server:client_id scopes; acceptance after an admin-configured trustedPeers relationship is by design.
